pipeline_stages.stage: 0. Archive the current English as 'old' BEFORE anything else
pipeline_stages.what: Snapshot compendium/en into 5-其他内容/english-baseline/<package>-<version>/ with the upstream version read from _source.json. This is step 0 of every upgrade cycle and the single point of failure for the whole method: without it, 'has the English changed' is unanswerable and every drift check silently degrades to a length heuristic. MUST be a FULL snapshot of every pack — this project snapshotted only 3 of 10 packs and three drift gates ran on 30% of the corpus for months while printing clean reports.

pipeline_stages.stage: 1. Define the mapping (declarative, single source of truth)
pipeline_stages.what: Write the Babele document-mapping layers ONCE, as data, in extract/mappings.mjs — shaped exactly like Babele's own default-mappings.js (keyed by document type; subtype keys like `JournalEntryPage.ember.location` are natively normalised into `_variants` by 2.9.1). The same data is consumed by two places: the runtime hands it to babele.registerMapping(), and the extractor INTERPRETS it to decide which LevelDB fields to pull. That guarantees the extracted English keys are by construction the keys Babele will look for. Cross-align it block-by-block against babele/script/mapping/default-mappings.js and record any deliberate deviation with a written reason so nobody 'helpfully' completes it later.
pipeline_stages.tooling: 3-常用脚本/extract/mappings.mjs (data) + 3-常用脚本/release/runtime-converters.js (translate-direction custom converters) + 3-常用脚本/release/generate_runtime.mjs (generates each plugin repo's babele-mappings.js). Any edit to either source file REQUIRES re-running generate_runtime.mjs.

pipeline_stages.stage: 2. Extract the English baseline from LevelDB packs
pipeline_stages.what: Walk each pack's LevelDB, apply the mapping, emit Babele-shaped <packageId>.<packName>.json into <repo>/compendium/en/ plus a _source.json recording packageId/packageVersion. Key allocation is modelled on Babele's own ExportKeys with one deliberate difference: two documents wanting the same key whose extracted content is identical COLLAPSE onto that key rather than the second falling back to _id. The English baseline goes INTO git (both Crucible-FR and this project do this) but is excluded from the release zip.
pipeline_stages.tooling: node 3-常用脚本/extract/extract_en.mjs --package <foundry pkg dir> --out <repo>/compendium/en [--target <layer>] [--pack <name>]  (requires classic-level resolvable from C:/Users/Taka/Desktop/fvtt)

pipeline_stages.stage: 3. Re-apply LOCAL-PATCHES, then verify by re-extract + per-leaf diff
pipeline_stages.what: Upstream typo fixes recorded in english-baseline/LOCAL-PATCHES.md are overwritten by every re-extract. Re-apply them, then re-extract and diff leaf-by-leaf to prove the register is complete — do NOT infer completeness from 'the gate is green'. This project found a 5th patch that had been applied-but-unregistered for four rounds while every gate stayed green; any re-extract would have silently reverted it.
pipeline_stages.tooling: manual + 3-常用脚本/qa/scan_en_drift.py as the verification diff

pipeline_stages.stage: 4. Compute the gap (three-way diff), separately for compendium and lang
pipeline_stages.what: compendium side: scan_en_drift.py old-EN vs new-EN, four buckets — `stale` (EN changed AND the Chinese length ratio fits the OLD English → re-translate, this is the main product), `changed` (EN changed but CN already fits the new EN → spot-check), `gone` (upstream deleted, CN still there → dead weight), `new` (translate normally). The stale discriminator: this corpus's CN/EN plain-text length ratio median is 0.31; compare CN/oldEN vs CN/newEN against 0.31. It cut crucible 295→44 and ember 921→280 on first run. lang side: lang_gap.py five buckets NEW / DRIFT / UNTRANSLATED / STALE / UNREACHABLE. ⚠ `stale` in scan_en_drift means 'CN did not keep up' while `STALE` in lang_gap means 'upstream deleted' — OPPOSITE meanings; the latter is called `gone` in scan_en_drift.
pipeline_stages.tooling: 3-常用脚本/qa/scan_en_drift.py · qa/lang_gap.py · qa/scan_content_coverage.py (fallback when there is no old baseline: uses the cross-language invariant that English digits must survive into the Chinese)

pipeline_stages.stage: 5. Subtract what Babele resolves for FREE
pipeline_stages.what: Run BEFORE handing anything to translators or you pay twice and create same-English-different-Chinese forks. Babele 2.9.1's DocumentConverter._genericTranslationSource scans every registered translated pack for one whose hasTranslation(data) is true, matching _id -> name -> sourceId, SCOPED BY DOCUMENT TYPE. In this project 352 of 371 nominally-untranslated campaign entries were resolved for free; the coverage number went from 'crucible 97% / ember 99%, 436 items missing' to a real residue of 19 items / 1556 chars.

Fill everything mechanically derivable first: fill_twin.py copies across twin packs where the English is byte-identical (12,560 entries / 8.17 M chars filled at 0 rejections, taking a pack from 0% to 90%); fill_missing.py fills leaves that do not EXIST on the Chinese side at all (a gap no other scan can see, because every other scan starts from 'the Chinese has a value'); fill_twin_names.py fills only EMPTY name slots and never overwrites. CRITICAL ORDERING: fix markup/alignment debt FIRST, then run TM fill — fill_twin abandons a fill when the markup does not match, and 66% of its 554 abandonments were exactly the pages a pending alignment batch was about to fix. Running it in the wrong order left thousands of entries unfilled. These scripts NEVER write compendium/cn directly; they emit a batch and go through apply_translations.py so the 8.17 M chars still pass all three gates.

pipeline_stages.stage: 7. Cut units for the parallel wave
pipeline_stages.what: 10–12 units per wave, 270–310 K English chars total (20–30 K per translator), paired 1:1 with adversarial reviewers plus 1 cross-unit term checker = 21–25 agents; that consumes most of one quota window. Large journals split by page-weight, small ones merged, non-journal content bucketed (tables / actors / scenes / items). Orphaned translations from renamed paths are attached as DRAFT reference (90% usable, 100% dangerous to paste — they were written against older English). CRITICAL FORMAT DECISION: for anything that already HAS Chinese, do not hand out a todo list that makes the agent re-emit whole values. Hand out PAGE FILES — <i>.en.html (read-only) + <i>.cn.html (a byte-exact copy of today's Chinese that the agent edits with the Edit tool) + index.json + _original_cn.json. This cut authored output from 1.45 M to 260 K chars, made 'bytes nobody touched stay untouched' a property of the format instead of a matter of discipline, and turned quota death from an accident into an ordinary interruption (12 agents all killed, 219 of 493 pages still done and gated).
pipeline_stages.tooling: 3-常用脚本/parallel/prep_units.py (split/merge/bucket/journals) · prep_realign.py · prep_sigfix.py · prep_catchup.py · attach_orphans.py · slice_todo.py

pipeline_stages.what: Every unit gets a translator agent and a separate reviewer agent whose default stance is 'this finding is a false positive'. Round 8 measured the reviewers: 136 findings survived, 63 overturned (32% overturn rate). Round 4 measured recall: a full sentence-by-sentence read of 35 journals produced 507 findings and the attached reviewers found 188 MORE (~73% single-pass recall) — and nearly all the misses were mechanisable, which is why a mechanical sweep must follow every human read. Translators self-gate to 0 rejections before delivering. NO agent except the controller may write compendium/cn.
pipeline_stages.tooling: Workflow tool with a UNITS array; briefs at 3-常用脚本/parallel/BRIEF.md (general), BRIEF-REALIGN.md (page-alignment batches), BRIEF-SIGFIX.md (markup-signature batches); lookup helper parallel/probe.py; residue self-check parallel/residue.py

pipeline_stages.what: apply_translations.py is a WHOLE-LEAF overwrite and parallel batches are all generated against the same base, so landing them in sequence lets later batches silently roll back earlier ones — measured at 350 contested paths in one round, 681 in another. Take compendium/cn's CURRENT value as base and replay each batch's edits as a diff. Real conflicts get written into resolutions.json with a stated reason and are adjudicated by hand (typical round: 43 batches, 681 paths, 24 multi-claimed, 20 auto-merged, 2 human calls).
pipeline_stages.tooling: 4-临时脚本/2026-08-12-fix/merge_batches.py --manifest <m.json> --scan then --merge --out-dir <merged>; manifest built by 2026-08-12-audit3/prep_manifest*.py; conflict-heavy rounds use gen_resolutions.py to draft 'superset + overlay' resolutions

pipeline_stages.stage: 10. Apply through the gate — never write compendium/cn by hand
pipeline_stages.what: Three gates, any failure rejects the whole entry: (a) the English source no longer matches the baseline (the pack moved under you); (b) no CJK in the value (unless the English holds no visible prose at all, e.g. a bare @Embed); (c) markup multiset mismatch — @X[...] targets, [[/cmd ...]] bodies, and tag-name counts must be identical, {label} is stripped first because labels ARE supposed to be translated. A fourth gate refuses to overwrite an existing Chinese value unless --force, and it walks EVERY level of the path, not just the leaf. Always --dry to 0 rejections first, then land.
pipeline_stages.tooling: 3-常用脚本/qa/apply_translations.py --repo <repo> --pack <pack.json> --batch <batch.json> [--dry] [--force]; lang side: qa/apply_lang.py with its own four gates (key must exist in the NEW English / placeholders {x} identical / HTML tags 1:1 / inline-markup TARGETS identical) plus a CJK requirement with a keep-english allowlist

pipeline_stages.stage: 11. Normalise style, then run the full QA suite
pipeline_stages.what: Quote/dash normalisation, then the §5.4 suite (see qa_discipline). Acceptance baseline: markup drift may only go DOWN, never up — if it went up, do not commit, investigate. Foreign-script contamination must be 0. For fill/catch-up batches, BLOCK and TRUNCATED must visibly DROP after landing; if they did not, the write did not happen (almost always a missing --force).
pipeline_stages.tooling: 4-临时脚本/2026-08-06/normalize_quotes.py --mode quotes|dashes --write · then the §5.4 command block · plus parallel/tagseq.py (positional block-skeleton diff — the gate's multiset comparison cannot see a block inserted in the WRONG PLACE) and parallel/prose_survival.py / diff_realign.py (did the translator quietly reword already-vetted Chinese? `~` opcodes are what reviewers scrutinise)

pipeline_stages.stage: 12. Commit, then smoke-test in a real world, then release
pipeline_stages.what: Two repos commit separately (plugin repo = translations; outer repo = docs + scripts). Smoke test is the ONLY thing scripts cannot prove — every static check is JSON comparison with Foundry never loaded. This project shipped every single version without it, and that remains its top-priority open item.
pipeline_stages.tooling: git in each plugin repo; smoke checklist in PROJECT.md §7 'as of round N'; console probes game.babele.inspectMapping(type) / await game.babele.sourceDiagnostics() / game.babele.cacheDiagnostics()

qa_discipline: THE CENTRAL PREMISE: all-green does not mean clean. The 0.9.2 release passed every §5.4 item at zero and the very next audit found 8 blocking defects in that same library. When the suite is all zero, the correct question is NOT 'is there anything left wrong' but 'WHICH CLASS OF ERROR STILL HAS NO CRITERION'. PROJECT.md §1 keeps a standing blind-spot table answering exactly that, ranked by value.

THE SCAN FAMILIES (the §5.4 pre-release suite, ~22 numbered items, run as one PowerShell block). Family A — lang channel: lang_gap five buckets all zero, especially UNREACHABLE (Chinese exists but Foundry cannot find it), plus flatten_lang's three-numbers-equal invariant. Family B — markup: scan_markup_drift (LINK/BLOCK/INLINE/PLACEHOLDER/TRUNCATED), scan_markup_targets (Chinese leaked inside brackets), scan_class_drift (functional classes the tag-name signature cannot see). Family C — content: scan_content_coverage (digits as cross-language invariant). Family D — contamination and dead weight: scan_foreign_script (must be 0), prune_dead (CN keys EN no longer has, plus keys with Chinese in the key NAME). Family E — the reverse direction: fill_missing (leaves absent on the Chinese side entirely — every other check starts from a Chinese value). Family F — link/label integrity: scan_uuid_swap, scan_label_vs_name (needs a per-repo id dump), scan_name_binding (needs a multi-package binding dump from LevelDB). Family G — cross-channel: lang vs compendium vs the runtime hard-coded .mjs, three grades of output (hard criterion / weak signal / no support, the latter two meaning 'a human should look', not 'this is wrong'). Family H — attributes: scan_attr_text (visible text in attribute VALUES; attribute NAMES translated to Chinese). Family I — naming consistency: scan_name_splits, scan_token_name, scan_bare_english_names, scan_status_name (compendium must match the lang status name CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER, not as a substring), scan_same_en_split. Family J — cross-version drift: scan_en_drift plus its three structural blind spots scan_dropped_terms / scan_number_drift / scan_marker_followup, all with coverage lines and --strict-coverage. Family K — the resolution gate: assert_resolutions.py (main gate) AND --selftest, both, always.

THE ACCEPTANCE RULE IS NOT 'EVERY ITEM ZERO', IT IS 'EVERY ITEM ZERO OR LANDING IN AN ARCHIVED EXEMPTION'. Two exemption registers, different shapes, never merged: a project-level EXCLUSIONS.json (uuid_swap / glossary pending / name_splits / per-leaf term exemptions) and a per-fork-group EXCLUSIONS.same_en_split.json (125 entries) that an assertion reads as RUNTIME INPUT. Saying 'all zero' pushes the next round into one of two errors: fixing legitimate forks, or waving real defects through as exemptions.

THE INVENT-A-CRITERION LOOP (round 8's method, 25 agents, the highest-yield round). Instead of running existing checks looking for residue, each agent INVENTS a class of error that has no criterion yet, writes a script for it, does a BIDIRECTIONAL BACKTEST — specificity by reading every hit by hand, sensitivity by INJECTING known defects into a TEMP COPY of the library (injectors never touch compendium/) — and then submits evidence. 12 probes reported 121 confirmed + 43 uncertain. Then 13 adversarial review agents re-judged everything with the DEFAULT STANCE 'this finding is a false positive': 136 survived, 63 overturned, a 32% overturn rate. Yields ranged from 1277 raw -> 9 confirmed to 24 -> 21; the low-precision ones still found real defects, and the criterion classes that survived (scan_status_name, the entity-anchored arm of pronoun-gender) were promoted into the standing suite.

'CAN THIS CRITERION BE BACKTESTED AT ALL' IS ITSELF A CRITERION. Failure shape (h) — the criterion is fine but the PROBE feeding it is fabricating input — was discovered only because someone tried to write a sensitivity backtest and found the probe was not reading the copy tree. If you cannot write a backtest for a criterion, do not trust its green.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW IS NON-OPTIONAL AND IS ALWAYS THE THING THE QUOTA KILLS. Translators run first and eat most of the window, so reviewers queue behind them and die. 'Batches are complete' therefore reads as 'this wave is done' when it is not. Never land without confirming the review actually ran — it is the only quality guarantee in the parallel pipeline. Reviewers must also keep their own progress ledger (append each finished page id to <unit>/_review_progress.json, read it at start, skip what is listed), because translators get resumability free from the gate and reviewers have no equivalent.

REVIEWERS ARE ALSO WRONG SOMETIMES. Of 188 reviewer-supplied additions, ~155 were accepted after independent verification and a batch was rejected — one had a false premise and applying it would have broken correct text. Two rejections were PARTIAL (other edits in the same leaf were right, only one spot was reverted).

MECHANICAL CHECKS CAN ONLY FALSIFY, NEVER PROVE. check_catchup passing means the digits and the length are there; it says nothing about whether the narrative, conditions and causality kept up. Content-defined batches must still be read against the English even when every mechanical check is green.

DECIDE THE COMPLETION SIGNAL BEFORE SENDING A BATCH, AND WRITE IT INTO THE PROMPT. The markup gate is a valid completion signal only when the defect is DEFINED ON MARKUP (block-count realignment: yes; signature mismatch: yes; content catch-up: NO — those entries' markup was already correct, so the gate reports 0 rejections before and after). A catch-up wave once had all 13 agents killed by quota having written nothing while the gate reported 'applied 378 / rejected 0'; only collect_realign's UNTOUCHED 378 exposed it.

JUDGE PROGRESS FROM DISK, NEVER FROM THE WORKFLOW RETURN VALUE. Two consecutive runs reported agents_error 13 / agents_done 0 — total failure by the return value — while actually advancing 219 then 422 of 493 pages. The return value is only populated when an agent returns normally.

REGISTER EVERY 'CRITERION IDLING' SHAPE YOU GET BURNED BY, IN ONE PLACE. This project's register has ten: (a) the criterion's own regex eaten by escaping; (b) it does not read the library at all (one assertion was green across four releases while 14 lang + 176 compendium violations sat under it); (c) it reads a stale report snapshot instead of the current library; (d) the gate runs but the exemption table is empty (or swallows the whole domain); (e) input missing but the criterion runs anyway, treating 'nothing to check' as 'pass'; (f) the regex is dead but the main gate is still green — only --selftest catches it; (g) input not missing but silently substituted (a .get(k, k) fallback compared a path that does not exist; symptom: the conclusion depends on cwd); (h) the criterion is fine, the probe feeding it is fabricating input; (i) the criterion ran and judged, but the conclusion never reached the door — 'skipped' was not counted as failure and rc stayed 0 while the screen was full of exceptions; (j) the criterion executed and returned, but its RULE TABLE was emptied — and its self-reported 'how much did I check' stays large. All ten report GREEN. A check that checks nothing while reporting green is worse than no check.

THE MOST EXPENSIVE SINGLE LINE: the anti-idling number must count 'HOW MANY RULES DID I JUDGE', not 'how many leaves did I scan'. Proof by two same-round injections: emptying a field list collapsed the detail from 'checked 1443 leaves' to 'checked 0 leaves' (visible), while emptying a forbidden-word list left 'English gate hit 244 leaves' byte-identical (invisible). Same guardrail hollowed out, one number collapses and one does not, and the difference is only what the number counts.

FIVE HARD CONSTRAINTS DERIVED FROM THOSE SHAPES: (1) never pass \b or \s through a rewriting script — Python turns \b into a backspace and the regex dies silently while the gate stays green; edit the file with an editor. (2) Write probes to disk and run them — bash heredocs eat backslashes and make the probe falsely green. (3) A probe's simulated input must point at the upstream contract that produces that shape; 'the data file has this field' does NOT imply 'the runtime hands you this field'. (4) Every conclusion a criterion computes must be traced to how it reaches the door — printed text, counters, and main()'s return code are three different things and have been observed contradicting each other. (5) Any probe that iterates 'one by one' must FIRST assert that the number of items it sliced equals a known true value and exit if it does not — this project mis-sliced five times (42 vs a true 212; 61 vs a true 74, which produced 16 fake 'no reds'), and every one was caught by that pre-assertion. The honest sentence attached: 'the probe did not error, it just measured the wrong thing' is now the highest-frequency failure mode, and only a known true value stops it.

BEFORE WRITING 'another gate covers this' IN A JUSTIFICATION, DO A PER-SITE MUTATION BACKTEST. Of three gates named as backup in one justification, one covered nothing and one was not even in the assertion set. Same class: before declaring something 'impossible / permanently unanswerable', run every available carrier past it (git history, release zips, someone else's snapshots) — that claim is just as falsifiable.

REGISTERING A FAILURE SHAPE CONFERS NO IMMUNITY TO IT. Shape (h) was re-committed in the very round that registered it; shape (g) recurred inside the criterion file itself, in a function sitting next to a docstring that names that exact pit. What produces immunity is a backtestable criterion, not a paragraph in a document.

STRENGTH PARAMETERS MUST NOT LIVE IN THE SAME LAYER AS THE CRITERION (a separate dimension from idling: the criterion IS running, its pass mark was just moved). Editing a recorded size from 19 back to 2 turned a gate that pinned 78 table entries into one that pinned nothing, with zero diff to library or criterion source.

EVERY ROUND'S FINDINGS MUST BE WRITTEN TO DISK, AND NOT INTO A GITIGNORED DIRECTORY. Anything a human adjudicated and that cannot be recomputed goes into 5-其他内容/findings/. This project lost visibility of 237 findings and 125 hand-adjudicated exemptions to a `4-临时脚本/**/*.json` ignore rule and had to rescue them later.

SMOKE TESTING IS THE ONE THING SCRIPTS CANNOT REPLACE and remains the project's #1 open item across every release. Console probes: game.babele.inspectMapping(<type>) should show your custom converters; inspectMapping with a subtype data payload should hit the subtype layer; await game.babele.sourceDiagnostics() shows each collection's translation sources and overlaps; game.babele.cacheDiagnostics(). Then check by eye: compendium entries render Chinese; after importing an adventure, items EMBEDDED in actors are Chinese too (this is the test of source-pack fallback); no TypeError in console. Every mapping-layer change, every runtime .mjs mechanism change and every enum-shaped field needs its own added checklist line.

Push main, create the tag, push the tag. The tag-triggered .github/workflows/release.yml verifies module.json version == tag, verifies the download URL matches the tag, (should) verify the changelog URL, builds module.zip and creates the release.

THE ZIP MUST BE REBUILT, NOT UPDATED. `zip -r` APPENDS to an existing archive. Leaving a stale module.zip in the repo shipped a 22 MB stale copy — including a corrupted translation file — to users. The workflow does `rm -f module.zip` first.

EXCLUSION LIST: compendium/en/* (the English baseline, ~22 MB, exists only to compute drift — shipping it doubles every user's download), lang/en.json (the lang_gap baseline, ~110 KB; also must NOT be declared in module.json `languages`, or a frozen snapshot silently overrides upstream's English forever), lang/lang_keep_english.json, release/*, .git/*, .github/*, .gitignore, *.zip, plus each repo's own maintenance-script paths. THE LISTS DIFFER PER REPO AND MUST NOT BE COPIED BETWEEN THEM: in one repo `scripts/` holds runtime esmodules that MUST ship, in the other `scripts/` is entirely maintenance code that must not. Copy the -x list from that repo's own release.yml, never from documentation.

POST-RELEASE: download the published artifact and verify it. manifest and zip both HTTP 200; then list members and assert the exclusions actually held. Use `unzip -Z1` (member names only), NOT `unzip -l` — the latter's first line is `Archive:  module.zip`, which matches a `\.zip$` pattern and makes the assertion fail against its own header. Write the assertion per-repo for the same reason as the exclusion list.
APPEND A ROW TO THE CHRONOLOGY IMMEDIATELY. This step was skipped 12 releases in a row and had to be back-filled from git tags plus module.json. Do it at release time, never in a batch later.

Fallback when Actions is unavailable: rm -f module.zip; zip -r module.zip . <the -x list copied from this repo's release.yml>; gh release create <tag> module.json module.zip --notes-file .github/release-body-template.md.

A release-time truth to state plainly in the release notes: 'the translations did not change this round' is not automatically true just because compendium/ and lang/ are untouched. A runtime .mjs change (this project trimmed a notification pattern table from 31 to 27 entries) is a USER-VISIBLE behaviour change — four notifications began showing English again — without touching a single compendium leaf.

pitfalls.pitfall: Windows glob returns backslashes, so a path.replace('/cn/','/en/') silently no-ops and the script compares the Chinese file against ITSELF
pitfalls.why: Produced a confident, completely wrong conclusion ('all 97 label-spacing cases are faithful to the English'). After switching to os.path.join the real answer was 6 genuine defects. The comparison never errored — it just compared two identical things.
pitfalls.guard: Every EN<->CN comparison script must FIRST assert that the two paths it resolved are not equal AND that their contents are not equal, and abort otherwise. Use os.path.join / pathlib, never string replacement on glob output.

pitfalls.pitfall: Term conclusions drawn from bare frequency counts, without an English gate
pitfalls.why: Both over- and under-counts. 25 hits of 电能 and 160 of 阶位 looked like leftovers of Electricity/Tier but the English was 'electrical energy' and 'Rank'. Conversely 167 hits of 闪电 contained only 23 real defects — 123 were faithful renderings of Lightning and 44 were metaphors. Acting on the bare count would have damaged 144 correct entries.
pitfalls.guard: Every term conclusion carries a three-bucket English-gated count (gated_hit / cn_only / en_only) via term_gate.py, and every rewrite goes through unify_terms.py, which changes an entry only when the English source actually contains the term. Never hand-edit around it.

pitfalls.pitfall: Whole-leaf overwrite silently rolls back parallel batches
pitfalls.why: apply_translations.py replaces the whole leaf, and all batches in a wave were generated against the same base. Landing them in order means whichever lands last wins. Measured: 350 contested paths in one round, 681 in another, 24 paths claimed by more than one agent.
pitfalls.guard: Mandatory three-way merge (merge_batches.py) using the CURRENT compendium/cn value as base, replaying each batch as a diff; real conflicts adjudicated by hand into resolutions.json with a written reason. Also: never give two agents overlapping path sets — when two defect classes overlap (32 shared pages), MERGE them into one task rather than splitting them across agents.

pitfalls.pitfall: Missing --force turns a whole wave into a silent no-op
pitfalls.why: Any batch targeting entries that already have Chinese (catch-up, fill, realign, term unification) is skipped by the 'existing Chinese' gate, reported as skipped(existing) rather than as an error. Eight fill units wrote nothing while overall coverage kept rising from other units in the same wave, so nothing looked wrong.
pitfalls.guard: --force on every such batch, and a post-landing acceptance criterion defined on the DEFECT, not on the gate: BLOCK / TRUNCATED must visibly drop. Markup drift may only go down, never up; if it went up, do not commit.

pitfalls.pitfall: Baseline missing a pack = that pack is silently never scanned, and the report looks identical to 'scanned, clean'
pitfalls.why: Three drift gates ran on 3 of 10 packs for months; 15,147 Chinese leaves never entered any of them. The reports were clean-looking the whole time.
pitfalls.guard: Every baseline-consuming script prints a coverage line (packs scanned / packs in repo / packs missing + how many Chinese leaves were excluded) and supports --strict-coverage to exit non-zero. Baseline capture must be a FULL snapshot, produced by a script that reads the version from _source.json, never a hand-copied directory.

pitfalls.pitfall: Re-extracting the English silently reverts locally applied upstream-typo patches
pitfalls.why: A patch had been applied but never registered in LOCAL-PATCHES.md and had sat that way for four rounds while every gate was green. Any re-extract would have reverted it with no signal.
pitfalls.guard: After re-extracting and re-applying, re-extract AGAIN and diff leaf-by-leaf to prove the patch register is complete. 'The gate is green' is not evidence that the register is complete.

pitfalls.pitfall: Comparing markup as an unordered multiset lets a block inserted in the WRONG PLACE pass with zero rejections
pitfalls.why: Counts are identical, only the order is wrong; players read a room's paragraphs scrambled.
pitfalls.guard: Run tagseq.py (positional block-skeleton diff via difflib) on realign-style batches. Note it also flags legitimate in-block word-order changes as MISMATCH, so read the opcodes rather than the count.

pitfalls.pitfall: The markup signature captures TAG NAMES ONLY, so functional class attributes are invisible to it
pitfalls.why: <ul class="complex-check"> and a bare <ul> are identical to the gate, and those classes decide whether GM text is hidden from players and how check results render. First measurement: 412 of 2214 class-bearing translated entries disagreed with the English.
pitfalls.guard: scan_class_drift.py as a separate standing check. And a related judgment error worth inheriting: a missing `section.block gamemaster` is NOT proof of a GM-content leak — in 36 cases the Chinese did not contain that GM content at all (a missing-block defect). Verify by searching the Chinese for that section's reference coordinate before concluding.

pitfalls.pitfall: Re-emitting a whole page washes away carefully reviewed prose
pitfalls.why: Every sentence goes back through the model and the wording inevitably drifts. Also, sizing units by the MISSING content under-estimated the real output by 5.6x (260 K estimated vs 1.45 M actually authored) and got agents killed mid-unit.
pitfalls.guard: The page-file format: give the agent a byte-exact copy of today's Chinese and require Edit-tool surgery, never Write. 'Untouched bytes stay untouched' becomes a property of the format. Then measure it with prose_survival.py and read the `~` opcodes in diff_realign.py.

pitfalls.pitfall: A half-written batch.json from a quota-killed agent gets picked up by the retry, producing something that is neither the old nor the new version
pitfalls.why: With the old batch.json format, completion granularity is the whole batch — you cannot see that 4 of 12 entries were written.
pitfalls.guard: Run batch_status.py before any resume and move incomplete batches aside (rename to batch.partial.bak, never delete). With the page-file format the opposite applies: leave everything in place, because completion is judged per page by the gate itself, so resume is purely incremental (measured: applied + rejected == page count in every unit).

pitfalls.pitfall: Semantic criteria that stop at 'co-occurs in the same leaf'
pitfalls.why: The first pronoun-gender criterion reported 160 findings, ALL false — the symmetric brother 26 : sister 26 count is the tell. The cause is always the same: there are several people in this leaf. Also, naive matching of a Chinese pronoun character sweeps in unrelated words containing it.
pitfalls.guard: Entity anchoring plus nearest-antecedent resolution. Use the source's own declarations (this corpus had 977 explicit '(NG, Name, he/him)' markers, harder than any inference) to type the proper nouns, then require the pronoun's nearest antecedent to be that person — that reached 0 false positives. Clean the token stream before judging.

pitfalls.pitfall: Numeric criteria anchored on Arabic digits are blind to Chinese numerals
pitfalls.why: 'lasts for six turns' rendered with a Chinese numeral, mistranslating Turn as Round, was missed by the probe's 21 hits and only found by a reviewer re-scanning independently. Conversely, forcing digit-for-digit coverage without folding Chinese numerals produced bad Chinese ('3 层矿井' from 16 correct instances of 三层矿井).
pitfalls.guard: Fold Chinese numerals (and multiplier words like decade/dozen) into Arabic before comparing, in BOTH directions.

pitfalls.pitfall: Coverage percentages counting entries Babele resolves for free as gaps
pitfalls.why: Reported 97% / 99% with 436 'missing' entries; translating them would have manufactured same-English-different-Chinese forks. In the campaign pack 352 of 371 nominally-missing entries were free-fallback resolutions and the real residue was 19 entries / 1556 chars.
pitfalls.guard: Always run resolve_generic_fallback.py before believing a coverage number or handing out work.

pitfalls.pitfall: The 'majority rendering' and the `name` field are both frequently the WRONG side
pitfalls.why: Of 153 label-vs-name disagreements, 41% were the name being wrong (a proper noun that had been machine-translated word-by-word). A 3:1 majority lost to an already-adjudicated decision. In another case 16 copies of a majority rendering all mistranslated 'scales using Dexterity'.
pitfalls.guard: Split-detection scripts report forks and give NO suggestion. Judge direction per group, and check whether that `name` is itself correct before using it as the top rung of the evidence ladder. Prefer the change with the smaller blast radius (rename 4 item entries rather than edit 126 prose sites) — but only after confirming which side is right.

pitfalls.pitfall: A fix applied to one copy leaves byte-identical siblings silently wrong forever
pitfalls.why: The same ability is copied verbatim into several packs. Upstream edits one copy's English; three-way diff surfaces only that copy. The others' English and Chinese remain mutually consistent — consistent with the OLD, wrong rule — and no scan can ever see them again.
pitfalls.guard: propagate_fix.py after every fixing round (push a fix onto byte-identical English siblings), and sync_twin_packs.py for standing forks between parallel packs (first run cleared 484 pre-existing forks that incremental tooling had never touched).

pitfalls.pitfall: Ordering error between the alignment fix and the TM cross-fill
pitfalls.why: fill_twin abandons a fill when the markup does not match; 66% of its 554 abandonments were exactly the pages a pending realignment batch was about to fix. Running the fill first left thousands of entries unfilled for no reason (re-running after the fix: abandonments 554 -> 143, 421 extra fills).
pitfalls.guard: Fix markup/alignment debt FIRST, then run the TM fill. General form: main line lands completely, THEN twin-pack sync runs last, because every main-line landing manufactures new twin forks.

pitfalls.pitfall: port_orphans moves PATHS, never TEXT
pitfalls.why: After an upstream rename the translation lands on the new path still containing the OLD name in its prose (a Lightning->Storm rename left 28 stale 闪电).
pitfalls.guard: After any rename-class drift, grep the library for the old name. That is what scan_renamed_terms.py automates (two detectors: an English tail that no longer exists anywhere in today's baseline; and a name present in the old baseline but absent from the current one whose Chinese rendering is still in the library).

pitfalls.pitfall: Adding a field to the mapping's translate direction without the extract direction (or vice versa), and adding fields that do not actually exist
pitfalls.why: An item's description key overwrote Babele's built-in default by key (mergeObject replaces a string with an object wholesale), silently zeroing ~766 K chars of one ruleset's content out of the pipeline while coverage still reported 100%. Separately, a field declared on the wrong document type idled in both directions for months (Actor.system.actions is a derived property that never enters toObject()).
pitfalls.guard: Both directions change in the same commit. Before declaring any field, MEASURE it in the LevelDB corpus and in both compendium/{en,cn} ('this field appears on 0 documents of that type'). And enumerate all string leaves in the packs, subtract the mapping's coverage set, and review the remainder — 'the field the extractor never extracted' was this project's single highest-yield blind-spot class.

pitfalls.pitfall: 'Everything is 100% translated' hides a whole enum field being translated as prose
pitfalls.why: A terrain enum id with `choices` was treated as body text, writing 104 Chinese values into document data — which breaks movement costs at runtime and throws console errors, while every static check is happy.
pitfalls.guard: Distinguish enum/id fields from prose fields in the mapping, and put every enum-shaped field on the smoke-test checklist — this class is only visible with Foundry actually loaded.

pitfalls.pitfall: A gate that validates at WRITE time can never see what entered before it existed
pitfalls.why: 357 entries / 791 K chars permanently violated the markup gate because they were written before the gate existed or while the English still looked different. Block-count measures could not see it — the damage was INSIDE the blocks (a dual-system <sup>/<sub> pair collapsed to one branch, so the other system's readers see nothing).
pitfalls.guard: Periodically run the gate's own criterion over the WHOLE library, not only over new writes. Note the second-order payoff: fixing that debt unblocked 15 term unifications that could not be written (their existing markup already failed the gate) and freed 713 K chars of twin-pack TM fill.

pitfalls.pitfall: Session-scoped scratchpad work is lost at a session boundary
pitfalls.why: Unit dirs and batches live in a per-session temp path and a new session cannot reach the old one, nor resume its workflow (runIds are session-local).
pitfalls.guard: Land and commit every batch before switching sessions. Keep all scripts and briefs in the repo so a new session is self-sufficient; re-prep by pointing an env var at the new scratchpad. The runbook is written to be read cold, deciding state from disk plus three status commands, never from memory.

pitfalls.pitfall: A scheduled wake-up lands on top of a still-running wave
pitfalls.why: A wave takes over an hour; writing compendium/cn while agents are reading it hands them half-written JSON.
pitfalls.guard: The first action on every wake-up is 'is a workflow still running'. If yes, report 'still running' and do nothing. Idling once is far safer than writing into a live wave.

pitfalls.pitfall: PowerShell/bash syntax bleed in documented command blocks
pitfalls.why: A line ending in `\` is a bash continuation but a PowerShell ParserError; 9 such historical lines had to be fixed at once. Separately, PowerShell writes batch files with a BOM, and the default console encoding raises UnicodeEncodeError on any script that prints a warning glyph.
pitfalls.guard: PowerShell continuation is a backtick. Readers of batch files use utf-8-sig. Prefix python invocations with PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 (or PYTHONUTF8=1).

pitfalls.pitfall: A scan that is not idempotent producing a batch that re-breaks already-correct data
pitfalls.why: A chained substitution table re-applied to an already-fixed library still reported '3 misalignments fixed' and emitted a batch that would have re-corrupted 7 correct entries. Its default output dir was also hard-coded to a long-dead session's scratchpad.
pitfalls.guard: Mark such scripts 'run only when there is an actual problem', add an idempotency guard (detect the already-correct value and exit without emitting), require an explicit --out-dir, and hand-verify every entry of such a batch before landing it.

pitfalls.pitfall: Two tools using the same word for opposite meanings
pitfalls.why: scan_en_drift's `stale` means 'the Chinese did not keep up'; lang_gap's `STALE` means 'upstream deleted it' (which scan_en_drift calls `gone`). Acting on the wrong one deletes live translations or re-translates dead ones.
pitfalls.guard: Rename one of them in the new project; if you cannot, document the disambiguation everywhere both appear.

pitfalls.pitfall: Adopting a wrong length-ratio band from documentation instead of measuring the corpus
pitfalls.why: A stale docstring said 0.4-0.7 was normal; the measured median for this corpus is 0.31 (suspect-inflation above 0.44, suspect-omission below 0.20, TRUNCATED at < 0.22). Using 0.4-0.7 flags almost every correct translation as anomalous.
pitfalls.guard: Measure the CN/EN plain-text length ratio on YOUR corpus before wiring any threshold, and grep out stale threshold values left in docstrings. Also remember length ratio is a candidate filter only — one known blocking defect sat at 0.377, squarely inside the normal band.

pitfalls.pitfall: Translating a page-title heading changes Foundry's slug and breaks every #anchor link into it
pitfalls.why: 234 @UUID[...#anchor] links broke at once because the anchor is derived from the heading text.
pitfalls.guard: Add explicit id= attributes to the headings (112 leaves here) — and put 'do the #anchor links actually jump' on the smoke-test list, because whether Foundry's TOC builder honours an explicit id can only be confirmed with a world open.

pitfalls.pitfall: Writing dotted top-level keys into lang/*.json whose values are nested objects
pitfalls.why: Foundry resolves a key by checking the WHOLE key first, then descending by dots. A top-level key 'A.B' whose value is {C: ...} satisfies neither path, so the translation is unreachable — 77% of one release's lang file was dead this way, and it shipped.
pitfalls.guard: flatten_lang.py before every release with the three-numbers-equal invariant, plus an UNREACHABLE bucket in lang_gap. Note the corollary: some UI strings genuinely cannot go in lang (upstream hard-codes them with no i18n key) and need a runtime patch channel instead — which then becomes a THIRD channel that must be cross-checked against the other two.

pitfalls.pitfall: A runtime notification/pattern table applied to a GLOBAL hook affects every other module
pitfalls.why: A regex table consumed by a wrapper around ui.notifications.notify runs against every notification any module emits. Its blast radius is far larger than tables scoped to your own windows.
pitfalls.guard: Scope runtime string patching as narrowly as possible; keep a gate that runs the SHIPPING translate functions in a node subprocess with negative cases ('must not eat prose', 'must not eat another module's notification') as well as positive ones; and require that every entry added to such a table comes with a test case, so adding one without a case turns the gate red by design.

pitfalls.pitfall: Directory naming and platform basics
pitfalls.why: Windows directory names cannot contain '/', so the project dir uses a hyphen. Node needs classic-level resolvable from a fixed anchor path. Some scans take 15-20 minutes and die under a default 2-minute timeout, which reads as a hang.
pitfalls.guard: Hyphenate. Pin the node anchor. Give the known-slow scans their own timeout or run them in the background, and record which ones they are.

module_skeleton_files: module.json — id, title, description, authors, version, url, manifest (…/releases/latest/download/module.json), download (…/releases/download/<TAG>/module.zip — must literally contain this release's tag), compatibility {minimum, verified, maximum: "14.999"}, esmodules: ["register.js", <optional runtime hard-coded-string patch .mjs>], languages: [{lang, name, path: "lang/cn.json"}], relationships.requires: [{id:"babele", type:"module", compatibility:{minimum:"2.9.1"}}, {id:<the translated package>, type:"module"|"system", compatibility:{minimum, verified}}] (a SYSTEM target goes under relationships.systems instead), styles: [{src, layer:"modules"}], bugs, changelog (…/releases/tag/<TAG>)

register.js — the registration entry point. Imports DOCUMENT_MAPPINGS and PROJECT_CONVERTERS from ./babele-mappings.js, and inside `Hooks.once('babele.init', …)` (NOT Foundry's `init` — Babele sets game.babele in its own init then synchronously calls babele.init) registers the converters and calls babele.registerMapping(DOCUMENT_MAPPINGS). Guard with `game.modules.get('babele')?.active`. Also the home for any Foundry/system data-shape shims.

babele-mappings.js — GENERATED, never hand-edited. Header names both source files and the regeneration command. Exports the converter functions and the DOCUMENT_MAPPINGS object keyed by document type, including subtype keys (`JournalEntryPage.<subtype>`, `RegionBehavior.<subtype>`) which Babele 2.9.1 normalises into _variants.

compendium/cn/<packageId>.<packName>.json — one per pack; the shipped translations. Plus optionally `<packageId>._packs-folders.json` to translate compendium FOLDER names (Babele recognises it by the collection name ending in ._packs-folders).

compendium/en/<packageId>.<packName>.json + compendium/en/_source.json — the English baseline. IN git (needed for every drift computation and for validate_translations), EXCLUDED from the release zip. _source.json records packageId/packageVersion so baseline snapshots can be named correctly. Note a pack with entries=0 will exist on the en side but not the cn side — that asymmetry is normal.
lang/cn.json — the Foundry i18n translations (the channel Babele does not cover).

lang/en.json — the archived English lang file, used as the OLD baseline by lang_gap.py / flatten_lang.py. IN git, EXCLUDED from the zip, and deliberately NOT declared in module.json's `languages` (declaring it would let a frozen snapshot override upstream's English forever).
lang/lang_keep_english.json — the allowlist of keys legitimately left in English (so the CJK gate does not reject them).
styles/<module>-cn.css — CJK font fallback and typography fixes; declared in module.json styles with layer:"modules".

scripts/<module>-hardcoded-cn.mjs (only if the upstream package hard-codes UI strings with no i18n key) — the third translation channel: a runtime patcher. If present it is an esmodule and MUST ship in the zip; that makes the repo's `scripts/` directory shippable, which is why per-repo zip exclusion lists must never be copied between repos.
selfcheck/ or scripts/<module>-cn-selfcheck.mjs (optional) — an in-world self-check panel. If two modules each carry a copy, add an assertion that the two files are byte-identical.
LICENSE (add one — this project's repos do not have one)

.github/workflows/release.yml — tag-triggered. Verifies module.json version == tag, verifies download URL contains the tag, verifies changelog URL == releases/tag/<tag>, then `rm -f module.zip` and `zip -r module.zip . -x <per-repo exclusion list>`, then creates the release.
